content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson focuses on **Installing Pandas**. Work through the listed subtopics (Checking the Python installation, Installing Pandas using pip, Installing Pandas using conda, Verifying the installed version) as decisions in one small data workflow: identify the input and its labels, choose the relevant Pandas operation, then inspect the output shape, values, and types. Do not assume the result is correct solely because the code ran.

content_blocks.expected_output: A successful installation prints a pandas version string; use the same interpreter for installation and execution.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run these commands in Windows PowerShell from the intended project directory. Use the same Python interpreter when installing dependencies and running a script. CodeLeaf displays commands but does not execute them on its server.
content_blocks.reset_steps: The example uses synthetic, in-memory values and does not modify project files. Restart the Python process or recreate the DataFrame to reset its state.

content_blocks.title: How to interpret the result
content_blocks.text: Compare the result with the task’s intended meaning. Check whether row order, labels, missing values, inferred dtypes, and duplicate keys should be preserved or changed. When the result depends on a library version or optional dependency, test against the environment you plan to use.

items.text: Use a tiny synthetic dataset to practise installing pandas and change one value, label, or edge case.

items.title: Verify the invariant
items.text: State the expected row count, key uniqueness, output dtype, or numerical result before running your solution.

items.title: Explain a limitation
items.text: Write one sentence identifying an assumption, a missing-data rule, a version concern, or a case where this operation is not suitable.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Avoid assuming inferred types are always correct, treating every repeated record as an error, or overlooking alignment by labels. Check the actual API documentation for the target version and assert the properties that matter to the task.

task: Practise installing pandas with a small synthetic DataFrame. Keep the input, transformation, and expected result explicit.
task_acceptance_criteria: The code uses an appropriate Pandas operation for the stated goal.
The result is checked for the expected values, labels, dtypes, row count, or alignment.
The solution documents a relevant edge case, assumption, or compatibility note.
hints: Start by printing the relevant shape, labels, and dtypes.
Write down the expected result for a tiny example before applying the operation to larger data.
Use a small assertion or comparison to verify the outcome instead of relying only on visual inspection.

common_mistakes.problem: Trusting a result because the statement ran without raising an exception.
common_mistakes.why: A valid expression can still select the wrong rows, misalign labels, or use an unsuitable dtype.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the output shape, labels, dtypes, and at least one expected value.

common_mistakes.problem: Using the operation without considering missing values or duplicate keys.
common_mistakes.why: Those records may change totals, group sizes, or join cardinality.
common_mistakes.fix: State the policy and test an example containing the relevant edge case.
